exposure: Histopathological features of Shallow Placental Implantation (SPI)
extravillous trophoblast (EVT) persistence in the decidua
extravillous trophoblast (EVT) persistence in the parenchyma
extravillous trophoblast (EVT) persistence in the membranes/chorionic disc
cohort: The study included 182 singleton placentas over 25 weeks of gestation submitted for histopathological examination.
finding: Shallow placental implantation (SPI) features significantly correlate with major obstetric conditions, lower birth weight, and placental vascular pathology, with parenchymal SPI showing the greatest clinical impact, especially on neonatal morbidities.
mod_finding: The presence of SPI features was significantly associated with Cesarean delivery (p = 0.007).
birth_weight: Birth weight was significantly lower when SPI features were present (p = 0.013).
gest_age: Placentas from pregnancies over 25 weeks of gestation were included.
